understand.concept: C++ integer types represent whole numbers with different ranges and sizes. Types include short, int, long, long long and their unsigned forms. Exact sizes depend on implementation, but minimum range requirements are defined.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct data declarations and type choices make C++ programs easier to understand, safer and more portable.
understand.explain: Use int for ordinary integer calculations unless a specific range or interface requires another type. Use unsigned only when non-negative semantics are genuinely needed; mixing signed and unsigned can produce surprising comparisons.

examples.title: Ordinary int
examples.explanation: int is a common choice for ordinary whole-number values.

examples.title: Long long
examples.explanation: A long long can represent a larger range than int; the LL suffix indicates a long-long literal.

examples.title: Unsigned value
examples.explanation: Unsigned types represent non-negative values and wrap modulo their range on arithmetic.

examples.title: Fixed-width option
examples.explanation: Fixed-width integer aliases are available when the implementation supports them.

examples.title: Avoid mixed-sign surprise
examples.explanation: Mixed signed/unsigned comparisons may convert operands; avoid this kind of comparison.
